documents.text:
Just Transition Northwest Indiana (JTNWI) and the undersigned residents of Eagle Creek
Township, Lake County, Indiana — Kristen Woodward — respectfully submit this comment on
Foundry Works Solar Energy LLC's September 3, 2026 request to waive MISO tariff provisions
and extend the Generator Interconnection Agreement commercial operation date from
December 15, 2027 to December 15, 2028.

JTNWI supports responsible battery storage when lawfully permitted. Ms. Woodward has
participated in and monitored local proceedings on energy and land-use approvals in the SR 2
and Clay Street corridor. We write together to supply local land-use and interconnection facts
that appear absent or understated in the waiver filing so that the Commission may evaluate
readiness on a complete record. That support does not extend to endorsing this waiver request;
we offer local facts for the Commission's consideration.

For context only: MISO Queue J1058 entered in 2018 as a solar interconnection request.
Foundry later replaced that request with battery storage while retaining the queue position. In
AES Indiana's IURC Cause No. 46394 (Monrovia Project), public utility testimony describes the
Foundry resource as a 200 MW battery acquired to serve large-load customer requirements,
including the Monrovia data center portfolio — not as a co-located solar facility. We cite this so
the Commission does not treat the waiver as concerning generic grid-greening storage
unrelated to the resource's stated commercial purpose. Our comment addresses process and
readiness, not the merits of data center load growth.

I. Local land-use status the filing omits or understates

Foundry's project connects to the grid through a gen-tie to NIPSCO's Dinwiddie substation at
State Road 2 (E. 181st Avenue) and Clay Street, Eagle Creek Township, Lake County, Indiana.
The battery itself is proposed on approximately 40 acres north of SR 2 on the east side of Clay
Street (Lake County Case 26-SE-06, Foundry Works Energy Storage LLC).

As of September 16, 2026, local approvals were not complete:

   1.​ Battery Special Exception (26-SE-06). The Lake County Planning Commission heard
       Case 26-SE-06 on September 16, 2026. The matter was continued (deferred) to October
       21, 2026 — it was not approved.

   2.​ Dinwiddie Substation Special Exception (26-SS-15). The Lake County Plan
       Commission held a study session only on September 16, 2026, for NIPSCO's
       high-voltage substation at SR 2 and Clay Street. As of September 21, 2026, county staff
       indicated NIPSCO had not filed the Special Exception application. Under county
       scheduling practice (applications due the 10th of the prior month for the next agenda),




                                                 1
        the earliest likely hearing is November 2026 if an application is filed by October 10,
       2026.

   3.​ Interconnection dependency. Foundry's ability to meet an extended commercial
       operation date depends on lawful completion of both the on-site battery land-use
       approvals and resolution of local land-use authorization for the Dinwiddie substation
       interconnection point. The September 3 filing describes NIPSCO as not opposing the
       waiver but does not disclose that the substation's local Special Exception track had not
       been initiated as of late September 2026.

   4.​ Enforcement context. Residents have reported county stop-work action related to
       substation construction in 2026, and county counsel acknowledged resident factual
       statements about sequencing of substation construction relative to local approvals at a
       July 2026 meeting. We ask the Commission to treat local land-use authorization for the
       interconnection point as unsettled unless and until NIPSCO completes the Special
       Exception process.

II. Inconsistencies between the waiver filing and subsequent local events

Foundry's September 3 filing states it was preparing the battery Special Exception and
anticipated local permitting completion in the fourth quarter of 2026. On September 16, 2026 —
thirteen days after the filing — the Plan Commission deferred Case 26-SE-06 without forwarding
it to the Board of Zoning Appeals, with further consideration scheduled for October 21, 2026.
That subsequent development calls into question the permitting timeline presented in the waiver
request and whether the project's current local approval status is consistent with the
development schedule on which the requested waiver is based.

Foundry attributes the delay to circumstances outside its control. The record also shows MISO
Queue J1058 entered in 2018 as a solar resource; no solar project was constructed in the
ensuing years; Foundry requested replacement with battery storage in late 2025; and Lake
County Council approved a Conditional Development rezone for the battery site on June 9,
2026 — substantially later than queue entry. These facts bear on whether forces outside
Foundry's control necessitate the requested extension.

The waiver request targets commercial operation by December 15, 2028. In AES Indiana's
IURC Cause No. 46394 (Monrovia Project), AES witness testimony filed April 22, 2026
describes the Foundry resource with a May 31, 2028 commercial operation target and notes
Foundry was seeking federal flexibility toward 2029. The Commission should have a consistent
picture of schedule expectations across proceedings.

III. Shared infrastructure at Dinwiddie




                                                2
 Public interconnection materials indicate other generation and storage projects are planned to
interconnect at the Dinwiddie 345-kV bus, including separate battery storage in MISO queue
J2215, with documented NIPSCO construction scheduling issues. We ask the Commission to
consider whether shared substation construction sequencing affects the realism of a December
15, 2028 commercial operation date for J1058.

IV. Questions for the Commission

We respectfully ask the Commission to evaluate:

   1.​ Whether Foundry has established that a one-year extension is necessitated by
       circumstances outside its control, given J1058's 2018 queue history, the 2025
       technology change, and 2026 local approval timelines;

   2.​ Whether December 15, 2028 is realistic given the October 21, 2026 continuation of the
       battery Special Exception and the unfiled Dinwiddie substation Special Exception as of
       late September 2026;

   3.​ Whether granting waiver relief before resolution of local land-use authorization at the
       battery site and gen-tie substation accurately reflects project readiness; and

   4.​ Whether shared Dinwiddie infrastructure dependencies identified in related
       interconnection queues affect the schedule Foundry presents.

We request that the Commission weigh the waiver request only after considering these local
permitting and interconnection facts.

Respectfully submitted,

Ashley Williams​
Executive Director​
Just Transition Northwest Indiana​
PO Box 8847​
Michigan City, Indiana 46361​
ashley@jtnwi.org
